land.text: the whole kingdom: all the Hawaiian Islands

successors.note: Monarchy overthrown 17 January 1893; the Provisional Government (17 January 1893 - 4 July 1894) is a state Cliopatria folds into this row's 1890-1894 shape, written by this group as its own dossier; it became the Republic of Hawaii on 4 July 1894 (Cliopatria's Republic row begins 1895).

capitals.name: Kailua-Kona (Kamakahonu)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Waikīkī / Honolulu / Kailua-Kona (following Kamehameha I's movements)' before 1820; Kona was Kamehameha's seat on Hawaiʻi island before the 1795 campaign (years are this dossier's reading).

capitals.name: Honolulu (Waikīkī)
capitals.note: The court moved to Oʻahu after Nuʻuanu; Kamehameha received Kaumualiʻi 'in Honolulu' in 1810 and 'after about 1812 ... returned from Oahu'. Years are this dossier's reading of the two pages.

capitals.name: Kailua-Kona (Kamakahonu)
capitals.note: 'After about 1812, Kamehameha returned from Oahu and spent the last years of his life at Kamakahonu'; died there 8 (or 14) May 1819.

rulers.name: Kamehameha I
rulers.note: Kamehameha page infobox: Aliʻi nui of Hawaiʻi 'July 1782 - 1795', King of the Hawaiian Islands '1795 - May 8, 1819'; sole ruler of Hawaiʻi island from Keōua's death in 1791.

rulers.name: Kaʻahumanu
rulers.title: Kuhina Nui (regent)
rulers.note: Infobox lists her as regent/Kuhina Nui 1819-1832 alongside Kamehameha II and III.

rulers.name: Kamehameha III (Kauikeaouli)
rulers.note: The page gives 1824 or 1825 for the accession.

correction.text: Hawaiʻi island alone, Kamehameha's kingdom after Keōua's death in 1791; shape unchanged, years 1791-1794

keyframe_review.note: The shape is Hawaiʻi island (bbox 156.0-154.7 W, 18.9-20.3 N; 11,830 km2 against the island's roughly 10,400 km2, fine). Only the years change: Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu were taken in 1795 ('in 1795, Kamehameha set sail with an armada of 960 war canoes'), so the next shape should begin in 1795, not 1796. No infobox area on any page opened.

correction.text: Hawaiʻi, Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi and Oʻahu; shape unchanged, years 1795-1809

keyframe_review.note: Right extent (bbox reaches Oʻahu at 158.3 W), wrong years at both ends: the conquest of Maui and Molokaʻi (Battle of Kawela) and Oʻahu (Nuʻuanu) is dated 1795 by the page, and Kauaʻi came in April 1810, so this shape holds 1795-1809.

correction.text: all the islands; shape unchanged, years 1810-1819, with Kauaʻi and Niʻihau drawn as a tributary (vassal tint) rather than direct territory

keyframe_review.note: Kauaʻi and Niʻihau joined 'In April 1810' when 'Kaumualiʻi met face to face with Kamehameha in Honolulu and negotiated a peaceful surrender': 'Kauaʻi became a tributary domain, and Kaumualiʻi stayed in power as governor'. The shape should begin in 1810 and Kauaʻi/Niʻihau should take the vassal tint until Kaumualiʻi's death on 26 May 1824 (ledger). Cliopatria's relation row '(Allegiance of Kingdom of Hawaï'i to British Empire) 1811-1819' is confirmed by no page opened (see notes).

All the Hawaiian Islands, unchanged 1820-1889; the page records no territorial change in these years. The British occupation of 25 February - 31 July 1843 is an occupation of the whole shape (ledger), not a border change. Kauaʻi passes from vassal tint to direct in 1824 (ledger).

correction.text: all the Hawaiian Islands; shape unchanged, years 1890-1893

keyframe_review.note: The monarchy was overthrown on 17 January 1893 ('Monarchy overthrown: January 17 1893'); 1893-1894 belong to the Provisional Government of Hawaii (its own dossier, new keyframe provisional-government-of-hawaii_1893), and the Republic of Hawaii from 4 July 1894 (Cliopatria's Republic row begins 1895).

ledger.note: 1791: Kamehameha becomes king of all Hawaiʻi island. 'When the Puʻukoholā Heiau was completed in 1791, Kamehameha invited Keōua to meet with him'; 'With Keōua dead, and his supporters captured or slain, Kamehameha became King of Hawaiʻi island.' Kamehameha had held Kona, Kohala and Hāmākua since 1782 (reign as aliʻi nui 'July 1782 - 1795'). Wikipedia dates the Hawaiian Kingdom itself to May 1795; Cliopatria and the Seshat Kamehameha polity start here.

region.text: Maui and Molokaʻi (Battle of Kawela) and Oʻahu (Battle of Nuʻuanu)

ledger.note: 1795: Kamehameha takes Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu. 'Seeing an opportunity, in 1795, Kamehameha set sail with an armada of 960 war canoes and 10,000 soldiers', 'quickly secured the lightly defended islands of Maui and Molokaʻi at the Battle of Kawela', then 'A fierce battle at Nuʻuanu ensued'. Kalanikūpule had taken Maui and Molokaʻi from Kāʻeokūlani in 1794. Month from the kingdom infobox 'Established: May 1795'.

1795: the Hawaiian Kingdom is established. Infobox 'Established: May 1795'; Kamehameha's reign as 'King of the Hawaiian Islands' runs '1795 - May 8, 1819'. Same ruler, same state, same colour (rule 2): the island kingdom of Hawaiʻi becomes the kingdom of the islands.

1810: Kauaʻi and Niʻihau submit as a tributary kingdom. 'In 1810, Kaumualiʻi met face to face with Kamehameha in Honolulu and negotiated a peaceful surrender'; Kamehameha 'was acknowledged as supreme ruler, Kauaʻi became a tributary domain, and Kaumualiʻi stayed in power as governor'. Unification page: 'In April 1810, Kamehameha I negotiated the peaceful unification of the islands with Kaumualiʻi', leaving him 'as a tributary king'.
1812: the court returns to Kailua-Kona. 'After about 1812, Kamehameha returned from Oahu and spent the last years of his life at Kamakahonu' in Kailua-Kona, where he died on 8 (or 14) May 1819.
1820: Lāhainā on Maui becomes the capital. Infobox 'Lāhainā (1820-1845)'.

1824: Kaumualiʻi dies and Kauaʻi's tributary standing ends. Seized by Kamehameha II 'On September 16, 1821' and held in Honolulu, forced to marry Kaʻahumanu, 'They remained officially married until his death on May 26, 1824'; his son Humehume 'attempted to reestablish the independence of Kauaʻi' and was captured. The page does not itself say when the tributary status formally lapsed; his death is taken as the date.
1824: Kauaʻi and Niʻihau pass under direct rule after Humehume's failed rising. Same page and wording as the vassal_end above; the gain converts the vassal tint to full colour.

region.text: the whole kingdom, 'ceding the land subject to any diplomatic resolution'

ledger.note: 1843: Lord George Paulet occupies the kingdom for Britain. 'Paulet arrived at Honolulu and requested an audience with King Kamehameha III on 11 February 1843'; 'On 25 February the agreement was signed ceding the land subject to any diplomatic resolution'. Counterpart: the United Kingdom (Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Great Britain' row, 1709-2024); the action was Paulet's own, disavowed by his admiral.

1843: Admiral Thomas restores Hawaiian sovereignty. 'On 31 July, with the arrival of American warships, Thomas informed Kamehameha III the occupation was over.' Kingdom page: independence recognised by France 17 March 1843, Britain 1 April 1843, and the Anglo-Franco Proclamation of 28 November 1843.

1893: the monarchy is overthrown and a Provisional Government proclaimed. 'Monarchy overthrown: January 17 1893'; a 13-member Committee of Safety under Henry E. Cooper proclaimed the Provisional Government with Sanford B. Dole as president. Kingdom page: 'The overthrow occurred on January 17, 1893.'

wars.name: Unification of Hawaii
belligerents: Kahekili II and Kalanikūpule (Maui and Oʻahu)

zones.text: Hawaiʻi island, divided after the Battle of Mokuʻōhai until Keōua's death in 1791

wars.outcome: Kamehameha unites the islands: Hawaiʻi island by 1791, Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu in 1795, Kauaʻi and Niʻihau by negotiation in April 1810 as a tributary domain.
wars.note: Steps: 'He achieved prominence in 1782, upon Kalaniʻōpuʻu's death' and won Mokuʻōhai; 'In 1790, while the aliʻi Kahekili II was on Oʻahu, Kamehameha's army invaded Maui' (Kepaniwai), but Maui was lost again and retaken in 1795; 'In 1794, the aged Kahekili II died' and Kalanikūpule killed Kāʻeokūlani; the spring 1796 and later Kauaʻi invasions were abandoned ('The second invasion of Kauaʻi was postponed'). Zones before 1791 are not drawn as contests: the rival chiefdoms have no dossier yet (report). Reviewer (oc-01): 'from' clipped from 1782 to 1791, this dossier's start (wars lie inside the life); the war began in 1782 with Kalaniʻōpuʻu's death and Mokuʻōhai.

wars.name: Paulet affair
wars.outcome: Five-month British occupation (25 February - 31 July 1843) ended by Admiral Richard Thomas; no border change; the ledger carries it as an occupation of the whole kingdom.
wars.note: 'the insubordinate five-month occupation of the Hawaiian Kingdom in 1843'.

certainty.note: Island coastlines throughout. The one soft element is status, not line: Kauaʻi and Niʻihau as Kaumualiʻi's tributary domain 1810-1824, and the disputed 'allegiance' to Britain 1811-1819 that Cliopatria records and no page opened confirms.

notes: Start year: Wikipedia dates the Hawaiian Kingdom to May 1795; Cliopatria's row and the Seshat polity us_kamehameha_k begin in 1791, when Kamehameha became sole ruler of Hawaiʻi island. This dossier keeps 1791 as the state's birth (same ruler, same state, no break) and records May 1795 as a rename; the reviewer may prefer to start at 1795 and treat the 1791 shape as a predecessor chiefdom. Cliopatria's relation row '(Allegiance of Kingdom of Hawaï'i to British Empire) 1811-1819' (the seed's relations[]) is confirmed by none of the five pages opened: the Kamehameha I and Paulet affair pages are silent on the 1794 Vancouver 'cession' and on any British protection before 1843, and the page 'Hawaii–United Kingdom relations' would not load (URL_NOT_FOUND; pages_failed). No vassal event to Britain is recorded. Counterparts without dossiers: Keōua's Kaʻū, Kahekili II / Kalanikūpule's Maui-Oʻahu kingdom and Kaumualiʻi's Kauaʻi (the pre-1810 Hawaiian chiefdoms) are named as the sources name them and listed in the report under counterparts_needing_dossiers. Region names: the gazetteer has no entries for the individual Hawaiian islands (only the state 'Hawaii'); radii around Hilo-side coordinates, Honolulu and Lihue stand in (gazetteer_names_needed: Hawaiʻi island, Maui Nui, Oʻahu, Kauaʻi and Niʻihau). Areas: no page opened gives an infobox area; Cliopatria's 24,850 km2 for all the islands and 11,830 km2 for Hawaiʻi island are plausible within a factor of two of the islands' land areas. Lāhainā coordinates are approximate. Update (oc-01 resume run): the counterparts of the 1795 gain and of the Kauaʻi vassal events are now the slugs kingdom-of-maui and kingdom-of-kauai, whose dossiers exist; Keōua's Kaʻū and Puna and Kahahana's Oʻahu still have none.
